Grace of An'she and Mu'sha is a sacred tauren pilgrimage undertaken on Red Cloud Mesa to honor the sun and moon as the celestial eyes of the Earthmother. By carrying fragile, smoldering incense to an elevated shrine in the southeastern hills, travelers show respect to the heavenly lights that bring warmth, life, and direction to the plains.

In tauren myth, the sun and the moon are known as An'she and Mu'sha, revered as the twin eyes of the Earthmother. While the elemental spirits dwell directly within the stones, winds, and waters of Azeroth, these celestial twins watch over the world from the heights of heaven. Their constant journey across the sky marks the eternal rhythm of day and night, granting warmth, guidance, and hope to all living creatures. Honoring the twins is an essential spiritual duty, teaching that balance requires reverence not only for the land beneath one's feet, but also for the light shining down from the sky.

To honor the celestial twins, a pilgrim must carry smoldering incense into the southeastern hills overlooking the mesa, nestled just south of the prickly quilboar grounds. The journey is an exercise in attentiveness and speed: the fragrant embers must be delivered before they burn away to cold ash, and travelers must take care to keep them away from water along the trail. Upon reaching the elevated shrine, the pilgrim casts the embers into the sacred fire, letting the aromatic smoke carry their respect up into the sky toward the sun and moon.

An'she and Mu'sha are the sun and the moon in tauren mythology, revered as the twin eyes of the Earthmother. Unlike the spirits of earth, air, fire, and water, they do not dwell directly within the soil of Azeroth. Instead, they illuminate the world from the firmament above, with An'she offering warmth and life, while Mu'sha provides nocturnal guidance and solace.

In the bustling coastal settlement, Caitlin waits in deep worry, clutching the woven reed heart to her chest in relief upon hearing that he survived and will soon return for a warm meal.

Crane Operator Bigglefuzz caused a clumsy cargo accident on the Ratchet docks, allowing a petty troublemaker named Mad Magglish to snatch a priceless vintage bottle. The vintage—a 99-Year-Old Port sent directly from Baron Revilgaz to Gazlowe—must be recovered from the shadows of the Wailing Caverns before the dockmaster fires the negligent crane operator.

Ratchet thrives on constant sea trade with Booty Bay across the Great Sea, but its goblin efficiency occasionally cracks under sheer volume. When an unusually massive morning shipment arrived at the port, Crane Operator Bigglefuzz tried to cut corners to speed up the unloading process. Lifting far more than his crane could manage, he dropped the entire haul across the docks. In the ensuing chaos, a local nuisance named Mad Magglish took advantage of the spilled crates, snatched a single valuable bottle of liquor, and fled inland.

The stolen cargo was far more than an ordinary ration of dockside spirits. The bottle was a 99-Year-Old Port sent as a personal diplomatic gift from Baron Revilgaz, the notorious Blackwater ruler of Booty Bay, to Gazlowe, the chief engineer and overseer of Ratchet. Losing such a lavish offering threatens to humiliate Bigglefuzz and enrage both trade moguls. Faced with losing his job or worse, Bigglefuzz tracked the thief to the ominous mouth of the Wailing Caverns, though fear kept him from following Magglish inside.

Rather than venturing deep into the corrupted dreamscape of the dungeon itself, Mad Magglish chose to hide within the sprawling, damp natural tunnels outside the inner gateway. Relying on clumsy stealth and dark alcoves, Magglish skulks through the subterranean caverns hoping pursuers will give up. Retrieving the port requires flushing out the thief from the outer reaches before the vintage is uncorked or destroyed.

The Great Outdoors is an introductory wilderness survival quest where the traveler Sam teaches fledgling adventurers the art of roughing it in the wild. By pausing to rest beside a basic campfire, travelers learn how to sustain themselves on the road before pursuing specialized tradeskills.

The wide lands of Azeroth call to countless restless souls seeking fortune, danger, and renown. Yet raw ambition alone cannot shield a fledgling adventurer from the biting cold or exhaustion of the open road. Mastering basic wilderness craft—knowing when to stop, build a fire, and gather one's strength—is the quiet foundation upon which every legendary journey is built. Sam's invitation offers newcomers a chance to pause and learn these essential outdoor survival habits.

Taking shelter beside a warm campfire does more than stave off the night chill; it provides a vital moment of recuperation known as boosted rest. Seasoned survivalists recognize that endurance in the wild depends on resting properly between expeditions. Once these survival basics are understood, craftsmen and gatherers can turn their attention to tradeskills, learning how to assemble dedicated camp fixtures tailored to their specific work out in the field.
